title: A Claude orchestrator is offered a tool to schedule its own wakeup, which would start a turn no driver records
foundBy: session agent, reading the claude-fault-lost-wake recording
details:
Recording the claude-fault-lost-wake scenario on Claude Code 2.1.283, the orchestrator's wait was moved to the background. The model then called `ScheduleWakeup` with a delay of 240 seconds, to check on the wait later. The call failed only because it named no prompt: `prompt` is required when `stop` is not true. The model ended its turn instead.

The tool exists for Claude Code's `/loop` mode. Whether a well-formed call outside that mode starts a turn has not been measured. If it does, the orchestrator wakes itself in a turn no driver records, the class the idle-orchestrator rule of SPEC.md R64 was written for. A delay past one wait chunk plus the settling window would also read `node-stuck` while the wakeup is still pending.

The next step is to measure a well-formed call in a member, and if it wakes, to disable the tool for campaign members.
